checkpoints.note: The attacker-controlled byte pair is accepted as a frame-sync candidate, so control leaves `SEARCH_FOR_FRAME_SYNC` and enters `read_frame_`, where CRC state is initialized from the current cursor.

First project-side statement that materializes attacker-controlled stream state used by the bug. After `frame_sync_` has already matched the leading `0xff`, this assignment records the second sync/header byte of a candidate frame and admits the parser into `read_frame_`, which immediately seeds CRC bookkeeping from the current bitreader cursor.

checkpoints.code: br->read_crc16 = FLAC__crc16_update_words32(br->buffer + br->crc16_offset, br->consumed_words - br->crc16_offset, br->read_crc16);
checkpoints.note: Missing wraparound guard. This bulk CRC call assumes `consumed_words >= crc16_offset`, but `FLAC__bitreader_clear()` can zero `consumed_words` without resetting `crc16_offset`. When the current resync scan later consumes only a smaller number of words, the unsigned subtraction underflows and the CRC helper reads out of bounds. The fix adds the missing predicate `if (br->consumed_words > br->crc16_offset)` around this call.
